label: Third original token (t=2) when the sequence starts with b/h/0/u/g
explanation: Fires almost only at step t=2 (99.7% of activation mass), the third original token, and is gated by the first original token: b, h, 0, u or g (each roughly 7x lift on prev2_tok). First token q gives weaker activations, e/f weaker still. Magnitude depends mostly on the first token: b-start sequences hold 53% of the mass, and the strongest activations (max) are for b z v. Sequences starting with g fire weakly and sometimes not at all. The token at t=2 itself matters little. Does not fire at t=0, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (aside from about 60 steps), and fires only rarely at t=1 or t=3. Misses are low-magnitude t=2 activations with other first tokens (2% of mass).

issues: Most factual claims hold on dev. 99.7% of activation mass is at t=2, and the feature never fires at t=0, the delimiter, or t>=6. There are 539 activations at t=1, 412 at t=3 and 63 in the copy phase, all at t=5. b-start sequences carry 53% of the mass. On test the reported scores reproduce exactly: P 0.956, R 0.889, F1 0.921, mass recall 0.979.
Precision of (t==2) & first_tok==X on dev: b 1.00, h 0.997, 0 0.992, u 0.944, g 0.843, q 0.239, e 0.119, f 0.074. This matches the stated ordering.

Systematic miss: the explanation says q-start sequences give 'weaker activations' everywhere, but q-start firing is actually set by the SECOND original token. For (t==2) & first_tok==q, precision is 1.00 for orig(1)=r or z, 0.96 for m and w, 0.93 for l, and 0.79 for k and p. It is 0.0 for almost every other second token (o 0.30, 2 0.30, d 0.04). This is a clean conjunctive class of about 3.4k active steps, roughly 4% of active steps, not scattered noise.

Systematic false positives: the second token also lowers precision for the listed first tokens. With orig(1)=c or v, precision for the base predicate falls to 0.71 and 0.61. For g-start with orig(1)=c it is 0.20, and for g with orig(1)=q it is 0.37. This is consistent with the profile's prev_tok lifts (z 2.3x, m/r/p 1.5x). The claim that 'the token at t=2 matters little' is true, but the explanation leaves out that the token at t=1 matters.

Adding the q-start case, restricted to those second tokens, raises test F1 from 0.921 to 0.941 (P 0.954, R 0.928, mass recall 0.988). Also allowing e/f with the same second tokens trades precision for recall (dev F1 0.931). Excluding c/v second tokens raises precision but lowers mass recall.
skeptic.revised_label: Third original token (t=2) when the first token is b/h/0/u/g, or when it is q and the second token is k/l/m/p/r/w/z
